issues.legal_issue: A High Court dealing with a reference arising from a judge’s disagreement with a jury verdict must consider the entire evidence, give due weight to the opinions of the judge and jury, and reach its own conclusion before deciding whether to uphold the verdict.
material_facts: The accused were tried by a jury, which returned a majority verdict of guilty.
The trial judge disagreed with the jury’s verdict and referred the case to the High Court.
The High Court considered only the objection to the jury charge, accepted the majority verdict, and convicted the accused without considering the entire evidence.
The Supreme Court held that it was not appropriate for it to consider the entire evidence in the first instance and remanded the case to the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court violated its statutory duty by accepting the jury verdict without considering the entire evidence; its convictions and sentences were set aside, and the case was remanded for the High Court to reconsider in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 307(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires the High Court, when dealing with a reference, to consider the entire evidence, give due weight to the opinions of the Sessions Judge and jury, and decide whether to acquit or convict. As stated in Akyhlakali Hayatalli v. The State of Bombay, applying Ramanugrah Singh v. The Emperor, if the evidence can properly support either view, the jury’s view must prevail; if no reasonable body of men could have reached the jury’s conclusion, the verdict may be disregarded. The High Court must assess the whole case under that standard.

predicates.jury_verdict_reference: A trial judge disagreed with a jury verdict and referred the case to a higher court for decision.
predicates.high_court_accepted_jury_verdict: The higher court accepted the jury’s verdict and convicted the accused.
predicates.high_court_did_not_consider_entire_evide: The higher court decided the reference without considering all the evidence in the case.

issues.definition: When a higher court accepts a jury verdict in a reference but has not considered the entire evidence, the conviction is set aside and the case is remanded.
